statement: For an i.i.d. nearest-neighbor elliptic space-time random walk in random environment in dimension $1+1$, is it false that for every sequence $M_N\to\infty$, every $\epsilon>0$, and every partition $\{Q_i^{(N)}\}_{i\geq1}$ of the transverse lattice $\mathbb Z$ into intervals of length $M_N$, the environment probability $$\mathbb P\!\left(\omega:\sum_{i\geq1}\left|P(X_N\in Q_i^{(N)})-P_\omega(X_N\in Q_i^{(N)})\right|>\epsilon\right)$$ decays faster than every power of $N$? Here $P$ and $P_\omega$ are the averaged and quenched laws, respectively.
